doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: The theatrical club and old performers in Chicago
summary: Mary describes a Chicago theatrical club managed by Jack L. Cooper, with Butterbeans and Susie and the Whitman sisters as veteran members.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You see, there were so many, uh, that has passed. Now, we have a theatrical chair club here.

Uh, I know who? We met at, uh, what's his name's house the other night? Uh, Jasper Taylor tells me about, tells me about that. We met, we met at his house, and Jack L. Cooper, well, he's our business manager, you know? Yes. And, uh, there's so many old performers there, but there's none as old as, hardly as us, you know, as together. But Butterbeams and Susie, and they are out of town, you see.
Oh, are they still, uh, around Chicago sometimes, or no? Yes. They live here. They live on.
I've seen them several times on the stage. Yeah. See Apollo Theater in New York, and once in Pittsburgh, too.
I think they're in Pittsburgh now, or something, they went to Pittsburgh.
Now the Whitman sisters, they're, they're about the oldest, and like us, you know. Uh-huh.
